# Eastside Trails

> Ride and hike finder for the Seattle Eastside (Washington, USA). It generates out-and-back, loop, lollipop and one-way routes from parking points, checked against a grade limit using USGS lidar elevation and, on an e-bike, against the land manager's e-bike rules. Coverage: about 35 miles around Newcastle, WA; default search circle 30 miles around downtown Bellevue.

Rides are generated in the browser by JavaScript (a web worker), so fetching the page HTML returns no rides. To get rides, give the user a link that opens the page with filters set (format below), or read the underlying data files.

Link format, all parameters in the URL fragment after `#`, starting with `v=` or `r=`:

- `v` what the person travels on (sets legality): `e1`, `e2`, `e3` (e-bike class), `bike` (no motor), `foot`
- `t` terrain preference: `paved`, `groomed` (paved plus groomed gravel), `gravel` (mostly gravel), `dirt` (mostly dirt trail), `any`
- `g` max sustained grade in percent over 100 m. The page offers three tiers plus any (`99`): 2/4/6 for bikes on paved or gravel, 6/10/15 for bikes on dirt, 8/15/25 on foot. Other values snap to the middle tier.
- `w` allow short walk-ups over the grade limit, value = max length in meters (bikes only)
- `min`, `max` route length in miles
- `at` search center as `lat,lon`; `name` its label; `rad` radius in miles (1 to 35)
- `r` a specific ride code. Codes are created by the page (Share button) and depend on the current map data build; don't construct them by hand.

Example, easy class 1 e-bike rides of 3 to 8 miles around Issaquah: `https://noghiri.github.io/eastside-trails/#v=e1&t=groomed&g=4&min=3&max=8&at=47.5301,-122.0326&name=Issaquah&rad=10`

Presets in the page: Easy ride = `v=e1&t=groomed&g=4`; Gravel ride = `v=e1&t=gravel`; Mountain bike = `v=bike&t=dirt&g=10`; E-MTB = `v=e1&t=dirt`; Hike = `v=foot&t=any&g=15`.

E-bike rules applied by land manager (each ride lists the rules it used, with sources): King County land, class 1 and 2 only on regional trails and paved pathways (KCC 7.12.315); WA DNR, WDFW and US Forest Service land, only trails and roads open to motor vehicles; WA State Parks, class 1 and 3 on trails that allow bikes, class 2 on park roads only; elsewhere the state defaults in RCW 46.61.710 (class 1/2 allowed on shared-use paths, no e-bikes on nonmotorized natural-surface trails unless the agency allows). Where no rule can be determined the ride says "e-bike rules unknown".

Caveats to pass on: parking points marked "unverified" were found automatically from OpenStreetMap; trail conditions and closures change, so check the linked agency page before going; paths with no access tags are assumed open except on golf courses, cemeteries, military land and airfields; elevation is 1 m lidar on bike paths and 10 m elsewhere (each ride says which).

## Data

- [Network index](https://noghiri.github.io/eastside-trails/net/index.json): tile list; `sources` (cited sources by key); `trails` (curated trails: managing authority and URL, surface summary, e-bike note, notes with kind closure/hazard/view/gap and a source key); code tables `flags` (bit 1 closed, 2 on-street, 4 dismount, 8 bridge), `surfaces` (index = code: paved, groomed, gravel, unknown, dirt), `access`, `agencies` (index = land manager code)
- [Network tiles](https://noghiri.github.io/eastside-trails/net/t/476_-1222.json): one file per 0.1 degree, named `<floor(lat*10)>_<floor(lon*10)>.json`. `edges`: `n` name, `h` OSM highway, `c` path/road/join, `s` surface code, `bk`/`ft` bike/foot access (0 no, 1 yes, 2 dismount, 3 unknown), `ba` 1 if bike access is assumed, `ow` bike one-way (1 along geometry, -1 against, 0 both), `f` flag bits, `ag` land manager code, `mo` open to motor vehicles (1 yes, 0 no, 2 unknown), `rt` 1 on a King County regional trail, `L` length m, `g` geometry as Google encoded polyline (precision 1e-6), `e` elevation deltas in decimeters at `st` m spacing (first value absolute), `r` elevation resolution m. `access`: parking points (name, lat, lon, address or null, pass, source key, `verified`, `tier` likely/possible for automatic ones). `pois`: toilets, water, viewpoints, trailheads.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/noghiri/eastside-trails/blob/main/README.md): sources and licenses, how the data is built, known limitations
- [Curated trail data](https://github.com/noghiri/eastside-trails/blob/main/data/curated.json): authority-sourced trailheads, closures, surfaces, e-bike notes, with source URLs and check dates

## Optional

- [Source code](https://github.com/noghiri/eastside-trails): pipeline (Python) and site (JavaScript); ride generation is in `docs/router.js`
